title: Painters Gainesville FL vs. Precision Paint Experts
description: Comparing Painters Gainesville FL and Precision Paint Experts for an older Gainesville home? What to ask about historic trim, wood siding, and period colors.
h1: Painters Gainesville FL vs. Precision Paint Experts
heroIntro: Older Gainesville houses have wood siding, layered trim, and decades of paint history. Before anyone puts a scraper to yours, run through the questions below with every bidder.

questions: How should old wood siding be prepared for paint?
What colors suit a historic Gainesville home?

body: Some Gainesville owners will have quotes from both Painters Gainesville FL and Precision Paint Experts on the kitchen table. We leave any judgment of the other company to you. This page is aimed at owners of older houses, where the condition of the wood under the paint drives the whole project.

Clapboard and lap siding, deep window casings, porch columns, and decorative trim all add up to a lot of edges and a lot of places for moisture to get in. Old layers may be cracked or loose in spots and sound in others. The quality of the prep plan decides how the new finish will age.

Many owners of older homes are also keen to keep original materials where they can. Replacing a whole run of siding is rarely necessary when a few boards have failed, and a careful contractor will show you photos of the problem areas so you can decide together. That is how our crew leads approach the walkthrough: document first, then recommend.

sections.h2: Questions specific to historic and older homes
body: Ask each painter these, then check that the written proposal actually answers them:
bullets: How will loose and failing paint be removed: scraping, sanding, or both?
If a clapboard, sill, or fascia board turns out to be rotten, who decides on replacing it, and in what form do you sign off?
Which primer goes on bare wood exposed during prep?
Is the work sprayed, brushed, or both, and is spray back-brushed into the laps?
What color guidance is offered for the home's style?

sections.h2: Our prep and coating plan for older wood
body: On an older Gainesville house, our crew lead goes elevation by elevation with a camera and a moisture meter, testing any clapboard that looks doubtful. The prep days that follow are itemized in the quote: the wash and mildew kill, scraping and sanding the old layers, resetting nail pops, rot and fascia replacement, new caulk, and primer on every bare patch.

Old wood siding and casings are finished in a 100% acrylic chosen from the top Sherwin-Williams or Benjamin Moore ranges. Weathered, thirsty boards often need a third coat on top of our standard two. Any section we spray is immediately worked by hand with a brush or roller, pressing the coating under each lap and into the grain. We describe the trouble signs we hunt for on that first visit in a post on rot hidden behind lap siding.

Older homes often look best in palettes that suit their era rather than whatever is trending. For inspiration, browse our roundup of period colors for Gainesville's historic houses; a Gainesville color consultation then tests the finalists as large painted panels right on your clapboards and casings. If you love the shade already there, we can reproduce it from a chip or a sample of the trim itself.
Porches deserve their own plan. Ceilings, floors, columns, and railings each need a different product, and the estimate should list them separately so nothing is skipped.

sections.h2: Schedule a walkthrough of your older home
body: Book an older home's exterior for the cooler, drier stretch between October and May if you can. Once washing and drying are done, the house itself usually takes three to seven working days, and our written workmanship guarantee on it extends up to 10 years. Request a free estimate or learn more about exterior painting in Gainesville.

faqs.q: Do you replace rotted siding boards before painting?
faqs.a: Yes. Failed boards and fascia are cut out and replaced during prep, never painted over. You will see each repair on its own line before you approve, and anything discovered mid-job waits for your written okay.

faqs.q: Do you spray or brush older wood siding?
faqs.a: That choice is made surface by surface on your house. Whenever a section of old siding is sprayed, a second painter trails right behind, back-brushing or back-rolling to drive the coating under the laps and deep into the wood.

faqs.q: Can you match a color from my existing trim?
faqs.a: Yes. A loose paint flake, a removable piece of trim, or an old can from the shed gives us enough to match, and you approve the result on a full-size drawdown.
